title: Randomized trial of low-dose, ultrasound-assisted thrombolysis or heparin for pulmonary embolism
summary: In 210 adults with intermediate-high-risk PE, this Danish multicenter RCT compared ultrasound-assisted catheter alteplase, IV alteplase, and heparin. Both thrombolysis arms used 20 mg over 6 hours. Thrombolysis improved CT clot-score reduction versus heparin by 3.6 points (95% CI 2.2–5.0); ultrasound assistance offered no advantage over IV delivery (difference −0.1, 95% CI −1.9 to 1.7).
findings: Ultrasound assistance did not improve the primary imaging result over IV alteplase.
No statistically established clinical-outcome advantage was reported in the abstract.
comparator: Heparin alone; catheter versus IV thrombolysis also compared.
population: Adults with acute intermediate-high-risk PE presenting to EDs in two Danish regions.
shortTitle: STRATIFY: ultrasound-assisted versus IV low-dose thrombolysis
limitations: Small trial with an imaging endpoint; not powered to establish mortality benefit. The abstract reports numerically more bleeding with thrombolysis but supplies no event counts.
intervention: Alteplase 20 mg over 6 hours, by ultrasound-assisted catheter or IV infusion.
whyItMatters: Clot clearance alone does not establish a reason to escalate a stable patient to thrombolysis or select catheter treatment.
evidenceNotes: Abstract reviewed; full text unavailable. Primary publisher verifies January 30; February 16 is typesetting, not first online. Abstract results and conclusion differ in their wording about death/bleeding; exact safety counts require full-text review. No separate correction/retraction found by DOI search. Later HI-PEITHO (NEJM DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2516567) found a clinical-composite benefit for catheter therapy versus anticoagulation in a differently selected population; it did not compare catheter with IV low-dose thrombolysis. Do not generalize STRATIFY to all catheter reperfusion strategies.
primaryEndpoint: Change in refined Modified Miller CT clot score at 48–96 hours.
